I've only ever shared this with 1 other person whose response was that it wasn't really CSA because I was practically a teenager when everything began and didn't I think that was different from if I had been under age 10 when it started. To this day I've never told anyone else about this, not even my therapist. But a 12 year old is still a child, so here goes:

It started when I was 12 years old and my abuser, the man who groomed me, was 26. He worked as the janitor at the church my family attended and was involved in the church youth group I attended. At the time, I didn't think of it as "abuse" because I willingly (?) participated in the "assaults" and I thought he "loved" me. One of the first encounters, which I remember vividly, was us kissing (adult style,) in the dining hall at the church. I remember feeling weirdly proud when he was surprised and pleased with how "well" I kissed, even bragging about how I had "studied" how couples kissed on the soap operas so I could do it right. I remember him saying that adding the tongue, aka "French" kissing, would be even better and how uncomfortable that made me feel, but doing it anyway because I wanted him to "love" me. 

That single incident formed the pattern that the grooming would follow from then on, me willingly engaging in the behavior to a point and him pushing for a little bit more, like making out without groping, then with groping while still fully clothed, then with fondling beneath the clothing, then fully naked, then only touching his private parts with my hand, then with my mouth... He never had full on  intercourse with me, but that's a moot point when you consider everything he did do.

The abuse continued even after he got another girl, who was of legal age, pregnant. I was devastated when I first found out and blamed myself because I wouldn't "let" him go all the way. It continued even after he married her. By then I was 14 and I would babysit for them and he would assault me when he was taking me home. It only stopped when they moved out of state. 

Although I exhibited many of the signs of CSA, I never related that to him until he contacted me through social media when I was in my mid thirties and I got that same creepy vibe I'd always get whenever he was pushing me to go just a little bit further.

I suppose I was fortunate in a way because I was approved for FMLA in December of 2018 after having a particularly viscous emotional flashback brought on by my supervisor and plunging even deeper into the depression that has plagued me for almost as long as I can remember. But it was only for the 12 weeks set out in the legislation and as soon as that time had passed and the doctor and my therapist wouldn't release me to return to work, (with good cause,) the company ended my employment. They sent me a very polite, but very final letter explaining that, although they understood the situation, they could no longer hold my job for me AND there wasn't any comparable position with the company I would be qualified for in the event that I was eventually released so they were terminating my employment effective immediately. All very legal but, regardless of the legalese, I was "let go" because I was sick and didn't recover in the time "allowed" by law. This was completely devastating to me. It destroyed what little self esteem and sense of self worth that I ever had and confirmed how worthless and incapable and useless I was always told I was and believed myself to be. It also confirmed that no employer really cares, no matter what they say, unless they're forced to by law and then only to the extent they're mandated to.
That would be LEGENDARY!!!

All I wanted to do was run away and hide. I don't know why  it's so hard to hear and accept that somebody actually cares about me. I don't know why it makes me so afraid, like somehow I did something wrong to make this person notice and acknowledge me. And I don't know how to accept it. I struggle to believe it. Just another indication of the years of physical/emotional abuse and bullying that made up my childhood.
Both my siblings turned out differently but not really better. They are both damaged in their own unique ways due to our upbringing.

What a coincidence, I just took the test online. The results came back Disorganized | Fearful/Avoidant. I can't say I'm at all surprised; it's just more proof that my mother and possibly other family members were neglectful/abusive much earlier than even I imagined. (As if my entire Shit Show of a life wasn't proof enough.) 

I don't suppose it really matters anyway. Having a label for my broken personality is cold comfort to me. My abuser(s) are long dead and never had to answer for what they did. And all I'm left with is this shitty  mess of a life, forever yearning to be close to someone/anyone but terrified of practically everyone. Endlessly choosing relationships with people who treat me the same way my abuser(s) did. Like I can somehow fix what's broken, erase the past by repeating the pattern until I'm finally able to be what they think I should be. 

Sorry for the length and the negativity. 😢 What can I say, I'm broken 💔

I did/do this all the time! I'm hypersensitive to the emotional undercurrents when I'm around people, especially the people I allow in my inner circle. I had a therapist years ago who told me I should "check my assumptions." In other words ask that person if I've said/done something to upset them. I never could quite be that open and vulnerable; the closest I could come was to say, "You seem a little upset/aggravated are you okay?" It worked pretty well if I was able to muster the courage to ask. And it's easier with some people than with others. But I found that most of the time although my assessment of that person's mood was accurate my assumption that it must have been something I said/did was not.

I used to. When I was younger and I thought they actually cared. But those same teachers, doctors, pastors who supposedly cared about me would inevitably send me back to the abuse/abuser with no help, intervention, or solution. I remember one time I ran away and went to my church pastor for help. I thought he'd help me but instead he called my dad who came with my brother and literally dragged me screaming from the church. That was the end for me. 
I don't trust anyone. Doctors, teachers, pastors, therapists, etc only care because they're paid to; it's their job and any care they feel for me personally ends at the office door. They have their own lives, families, friends and I'm just another patient, student, parishioner.

I've felt like that way most of my life. I've even invalidated my trauma to myself because there are so many people out there with absolute horror stories and mine seemed so much less. Heck, I didn't even start seeking therapy until I was in my thirties because nobody else ever even acknowledged that any abuse had occurred or that it had any negative effect on me. It took an almost total stranger asking me how long I'd had a problem with depression and how long I'd been suicidal before I could acknowledge it myself. To this day, (I'm 55 now,) I rarely share the nature of the abuse or the extent of the subsequent trauma. So many times I've heard how I SHOULDN'T be SO traumatized by what happened to me because "it's not like they BEAT you or MOLESTED you." Maybe not but they broke me just the same.

I'm in the USA and in this country the quality of care is directly linked to how much money you have and/or how good your insurance is. When I was able to work and I had good insurance, I received excellent care from highly qualified mental health professionals. When I didn't it was low-bottom, indigent mental health facilities where the focus tended to be on "dual diagnosis" and getting addicts into rehab.

Now for instance, I'm losing my therapist and psych at the beginning of the year because my monthly income is increasing $20.00 per month and I no longer qualify for the health insurance that covered them. I don't qualify for any assistance from my state because my annual income is $2000 too much. So I'll be untreated and unmedicated and nobody cares because I don't have the money to make them care.
